clue.text: Fellow has hankering to get a paint-brush

parts.note: a hankering is an itch, a restless longing

explanation.surface: A man longs to get his hands on a brush and start painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitch is an artist's brush, originally made from polecat hair.

clue.text: Trustee-— fraud in city is out — isn't dismissed

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of this word are the ones dismissed from the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A trustee is exposed for fraud in the City and duly sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 13 letters of FRAUD IN CITY IS are rearranged ('out') after the letters of ISN'T are 'dismissed' from the pool, leaving nine letters to spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiduciary is a person holding property or power in trust for another.

clue.text: The Thunderer has a point, a painful one

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The Thunderer (The Times's old nickname) makes a point that hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thunderer' was a nickname of The Times itself, but here it is the Norse god. 'One' in the definition stands for 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickle that pierces the skin is a sharp point that hurts.

clue.text: Happy toil of Hercules involved her

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheerful labour of Hercules that brought in a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges HAPPY TOIL. The words 'of Hercules' tell you who 'her' is: the Amazon queen whose girdle Hercules had to win as one of his labours.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippolyta was the Amazon queen whose belt Hercules was sent to fetch, a woman in his story.

clue.text: A let down if it opens — or doesn't

definitions.text: A let down if it opens — or doesn't

parts.words: A let down if it opens — or doesn't
parts.note: a skydiver's canopy lowers you gently when it unfurls, and is a grave disappointment when it fails to

explanation.surface: Something that disappoints whether or not it gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: The canopy lets a jumper down safely when it opens; failing to open is the worst let-down of all.

clue.text: Assumed to have adopted attitude about it

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the pose wraps the little word

parts.note: to adopt an attitude is to pose; past tense gives posed

explanation.surface: Someone was presumed to have struck a pose over something.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit something is to put it forward as true without proof, to suppose it.

clue.text: Colourful way Apollo warned the shepherds

definitions.meaning: Apollo is the sun god; 'red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning', so the sun came up red

explanation.surface: A vivid description of how the sun god gave herdsmen fair warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The old saying is 'red sky at night, shepherd's delight; red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinkish crimson tint is vivid, and the sun god's sun came up crimson at dawn, the shepherds' omen of bad weather.

clue.text: Can turn over in the mind

definitions.meaning: to go over a matter again and again, mulling it

explanation.surface: Is it possible to keep mulling something over?
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy's tall milk vessel; and to keep thoughts revolving, worrying at them.

clue.text: Patriotism In the interior

definitions.meaning: the cry 'up (with our) country!' sums up love of one's nation

explanation.surface: Love of one's nation found deep in the heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland regions away from the coast; split, the words read as a cheer for the nation.

clue.text: No ball for such a dumb actor

definitions.meaning: in cricket an illegal delivery, which adds a run not credited to the batsman
a non-speaking film or stage performer, a walk-on

explanation.surface: Without a ball, a speechless performer is left in the lurch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is a delivery bowled illegally; the penalty run it gives is one of the bonus runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-ball's penalty run is a bonus run in cricket's scoring, and a walk-on with no lines is a supernumerary.

clue.text: Between the two of them bride is carried over threshold

definitions.text: Between the two of them bride is carried over threshold

parts.words: Between the two of them bride is carried over threshold
parts.note: the uprights on either side of an entrance, which the groom passes between with his new wife in his arms

explanation.surface: A newly married couple: he carries her into their home.
explanation.definitionFit: The two vertical members framing an entrance, between which the bride is carried.

clue.text: But so rough a diamond is not rudely ignored

definitions.meaning: a gem straight from the mine, not yet shaped by a lapidary
to cut someone is to snub them, so someone not snubbed

explanation.surface: Someone a little rough round the edges still is not snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough diamond' suggests a coarse but decent person, but here it is a gem not yet faceted.
explanation.definitionFit: An unworked gemstone has not been faceted; and someone who has not been cut, that is snubbed.

clue.text: Trick is to take leave here in Africa

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
to take leave is to go away

explanation.surface: The scam is to bow out somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a central African river and the countries named after it.

clue.text: Horrid creature leaving poor aunt in embarrassing altar situation

indicators.note: in places the first jumble inside the second
an embarrassing situation is a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder
poor suggests the word is in bad shape, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A nasty spider scuttles away from an unfortunate relative stuck in an awkward wedding scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges AUNT into ANTU, and 'embarrassing' rearranges ALTAR into TARLA; 'in' puts ANTU inside TARLA after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy spider, the sort of creepy-crawly many find frightful.

clue.text: Beam in a colour feature as ordered

indicators.note: in places the shaft of light inside the hue

parts.note: red is a colour
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A shaft of light is placed in a coloured feature as instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops set out in ranks are drawn up in order, arranged.

clue.text: Hope king had a stand-in for coronation here

definitions.text: Hope king had a stand-in for coronation here

parts.words: Hope king had a stand-in for coronation here
parts.note: Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda has a lookalike crowned in place of the kidnapped king of an imaginary country

explanation.surface: One hopes the monarch had an understudy for his crowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' looks like a verb but is the novelist Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Central European kingdom in which Hope set The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Pointer in astronavigation ?

parts.note: a pointer is a breed of hunting dog; Sirius, the brightest star, bears a canine name and guided navigators

explanation.surface: A guide used for finding your way by the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, in the constellation Canis Major, is nicknamed after a hound, the 'pointer' of the clue.

clue.text: Sling folk out for playing by the sea

indicators.note: out suggests the words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw the locals out so we can play at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are seaside golf courses on sandy coastal ground, laid out for playing.

clue.text: Ginger's description of cattle ?

parts.note: ginger suggests a red head; cattle bred without horns are called polled, so russet hornless beasts

explanation.surface: How a red-haired person called Ginger might describe livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' is a nickname for a red-haired person, but here it just means red; 'polled' cattle are hornless.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornless breed of russet cattle carries this name, so it describes beasts that are red and polled.

clue.text: Not long one of the law? It could be rigged

definitions.text: Not long one of the law?
definitions.meaning: the long arm of the law, but one belonging to Scotland Yard, three feet long
a spar on a sailing ship's mast, part of the rigging

explanation.surface: A short-reaching police officer, perhaps open to fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters; a yard is three feet, so not a 'long' arm. 'Rigged' sounds like fixed but means fitted with rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal spar on a ship's mast, from which sails are hung, read playfully as a short police limb.

clue.text: Lover and his lass ? Sounds so artificial

indicators.note: sounds means the phrase before is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a lover and his lass are a man and a maid

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean pair of young lovers; it all rings rather fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was a lover and his lass' is a song from As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manufactured rather than natural is synthetic, made by people.

clue.text: Assuaged, everyone agreed with skipper

parts.note: all means everyone
sailors answer the captain 'aye aye', so to agree with the skipper is to have said aye

explanation.surface: All was calmed once the crew agreed with their captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage fears is to calm or soothe them, to quieten them.

clue.text: A cricketer's holding it up in defence

indicators.note: holding means the batsman's letters enclose another piece

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket; with the 's it gives bats

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A batsman is stonewalling, blocking everything in a defensive innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns IT into TI, and 'holding' puts TI inside BAT'S after BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An abatis is a barricade of felled trees with sharpened branches laid toward an enemy, a military obstacle.

clue.text: Part of old Spain, see, in Sicilian port

indicators.note: in places the old exclamation inside the city name

parts.note: Catania is a port on Sicily's east coast
lo is an old word for see, look

explanation.surface: Look, a region of Spain is found within a port in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern region round Barcelona was historically a principality within Aragon, part of Spain.

clue.text: No gentleman soldier in this group

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, no gentleman
RE, the Royal Engineers, stand for a soldier

explanation.surface: Within this unit there is no gentlemanly soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core unit of trained people, especially in an army or party.

clue.text: Confine one monsieur in his place of retirement

indicators.note: in places one and monsieur inside the bed

parts.note: the Frenchman's bed is a lit; one retires to bed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is shut up in his retirement home.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict it within bounds.

clue.text: Catch girl with nothing on

indicators.note: on means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Seize a young woman wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A noosed rope is thrown to catch cattle or horses.

clue.text: Period of charm

definitions.meaning: a stretch of time, a while

explanation.surface: A time of enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of time; and a magic incantation that enchants.

clue.text: Got coal in return for such material

indicators.note: in return means the letters come back, read from right to left

parts.note: to get coal is to mine it, so mined

explanation.surface: Coal dug in exchange for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: London beauty announced literary pseudonym

parts.note: Acton is a district of West London

indicators.note: announced means the word for beauty is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A London beauty is named as a writer's pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London. Anne Brontë published under this pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë wrote Agnes Grey under this male pen name.

clue.text: Repealed law having point and precision

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in force
an act is a law passed by parliament
a ness is a headland, a point of land

explanation.surface: A struck-down statute that had a point and accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is accuracy, being correct in every detail.

clue.text: Thus the cover is sound

parts.note: so means thus
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: So the lid fits well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm and dependable is sound, well-founded and reliable.
